entry: Island in western [[Indonesia]], the largest island fully within Indonesian territory and the sixth-largest in the world, at 482,286.55 sq km including adjacent islands and archipelagos. Its elongated landmass spans a northwest–southeast axis, with the [[Equator|equator]] crossing near its center. The Bukit Barisan mountains form its backbone, and the island is seismically active, the site of several of the largest volcanic eruptions and earthquakes in history. Deforestation and industrial agriculture have degraded its rain forest ecosystems and caused severe seasonal haze. Sumatra was the center of major regional powers, including the [[Srivijaya|Srivijaya Empire]] and the Aceh Sultanate, and its trading ports helped spread [[Islam]] across Southeast Asia. Its population of around 62 million includes many Indigenous and other ethnic groups who speak more than 52 languages.

Ancient language of [[Mesopotamia]], the oldest attested language, dating back to at least 3100 BC. It is a language isolate, unrelated to any other known language, spoken in the area of modern [[Iraq]] and written in [[Cuneiform|cuneiform]] script. [[Akkadian language|Akkadian]], a Semitic language, gradually replaced Sumerian as the primary spoken language around c. 2000 BC, but Sumerian remained a sacred, ceremonial, literary and scientific language in Akkadian-speaking states such as [[Assyria]] and [[Babylonia]] until the 1st century AD. The cuneiform script, originally developed for Sumerian, was adopted by many regional languages, and Akkadian's grammar and vocabulary were significantly influenced by Sumerian. Scholars began deciphering its inscriptions in the 19th century.

Unfinished theological treatise by Thomas Aquinas, a compendium of the main teachings of the [[Catholic Church]]. Its topics follow a cycle of God, creation, man, Christ, the sacraments and back to God, and it is divided into three parts with 614 questions and 3,125 articles. Aquinas aims to reconcile [[Aristotle]]'s philosophy with Catholic theology, calling him "the philosopher" and drawing broadly on the [[Bible]]. A more structured expansion of his earlier *Summa contra Gentiles*, it was one of the main inspirations for Thomistic philosophy. Its influence on [[Dante Alighieri]]'s *Divine Comedy* led the poem to be called "the Summa in verse." It remains a major reference in the Western and Eastern Catholic Churches and in mainline Protestant denominations, including Anglicanism and Lutheranism.

Addition of a sequence of numbers, or of other values such as [[Function (mathematics)|functions]], vectors and matrices. The numbers added are called addends or summands, and the result is their sum. Because addition is associative and commutative, no parentheses are needed, and the empty sum is 0 by convention. Long regular sums are written with ellipses or Σ (sigma) notation. Summations of infinite sequences are called [[Series (mathematics)|series]] and involve the concept of [[Limit (mathematics)|limit]].

Hottest and brightest of the four temperate seasons, occurring between [[Spring (season)|spring]] and [[Autumn|autumn]]. Starting at or around the [[Summer solstice|summer solstice]], daylight hours are longest and darkness shortest. In the Northern Hemisphere, summer is usually defined as June 21 or 22 to September 22 or 23; in the Southern Hemisphere, December 22 or 23 to March 20 or 21. Meteorologists instead use June, July and August in the north and December, January and February in the south, a convention used in Australia, New Zealand, Austria, Denmark, Russia and Japan. The English word derives from Middle English *somer*, via Old English *sumor*. In the [[Julian calendar]] of the ancient Roman world, summer ran from May 9 to August 10, with the solstice on June 24 at its midpoint.

Major international multi-sport event, normally held once every four years. The first Games took place in 1896 in [[Athens]], Greece, and were organized by the International Olympic Committee, founded by [[Pierre de Coubertin]]. Medals have been awarded since 1904. The Games grew from 42 events in 1896, with fewer than 250 male competitors from 14 nations, to 339 events in 2021 with 11,319 competitors from 206 nations. They have been held in nineteen countries over five continents. The United States leads the all-time medal count and has topped the medal table 19 times. [[London]] and [[Paris]] have each hosted three times. The Summer Games are regarded as the largest and most prestigious multi-sport event in the world, and the [[Winter Olympic Games]] were created out of their success.

Astronomical moment when one of Earth's poles reaches its maximum tilt toward the Sun. It occurs twice yearly, in June in the Northern Hemisphere and in December in the Southern, and marks the longest day of daylight in that hemisphere. At either pole there is continuous daylight at this time. Earth's maximum axial tilt is 23.44°, and the event has been marked by festivals and rituals since prehistory. In the [[Julian calendar]] of the Roman Empire it fell on June 24. The [[First Council of Nicaea]] (325) set the spring equinox at March 21, which moved the solstice forward to June 20.

Japanese form of competitive full-contact wrestling, the national sport of [[Japan]] and the only country where it is practiced professionally. A *rikishi* (wrestler) tries to force an opponent out of a *dohyō* (circular ring) or to touch the ground with any body part other than the soles of the feet. Wrestlers live in communal training stables, or *heya*, under rules set by the Japan Sumo Association, and daily life follows strict tradition. Many ritual elements survive from [[Shinto]], including salt purification. Wrestlers have a much lower [[Life expectancy|life expectancy]] than the average Japanese man. The sport is first mentioned in the [[Kojiki]] manuscript of 712. Six annual 15-day tournaments are held in [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka]], [[Nagoya]] and [[Fukuoka]].

Chinese general, strategist and writer traditionally credited as the author of *The Art of War*. Traditional histories place him as a minister to King Helü of Wu, and say he led Wu to victory over the much larger state of Chu at the Battle of Boju in 506 BC. The earliest biography, in [[Sima Qian]]'s *Shiji*, was written around 97 BC; the scholar Mair calls it "essentially fictional." Scholars from the [[Song dynasty]] doubted his existence, noting that the *Zuo Zhuan* never mentions him. The text is a [[Military strategy|military strategy]] treatise probably compiled in the [[Warring States period]], and its earliest parts may date to at least a century after him. His descendant Sun Bin is said to have written a treatise on tactics with the same title, and until its rediscovery in 1972 some historians thought the two men were identical.

Monkey King of Chinese mythology, a main character of the 16th-century novel [[Journey to the West]]. Born from a stone, he acquires supernatural powers through Taoist practices and heavenly food. After rebelling against heaven, he is imprisoned under a mountain by the Buddha, and five hundred years later he accompanies the monk Tang Sanzang to obtain Buddhist sutras. He has supernatural strength, can travel 108,000 li in one somersault, and acquires 72 Earthly Transformations. Art historian Wu Hung argues that some early visual prototypes of the legend appear on Eastern Han dynasty stone carvings from Sichuan, including scenes of an ape abducting a woman. Hu Shih suggested that the author may have been influenced by the Hindu deity [[Hanuman]] of the [[Ramayana]]. Other scholars dispute Wu's reading of the carvings.

Chinese physician and revolutionary who founded the Republic of China. He led the [[1911 Revolution]] that overthrew the [[Qing dynasty]], and as the first provisional president of the Republic in 1912 he relinquished the presidency to Yuan Shikai to secure the Qing court's abdication. He founded the [[Kuomintang]] and led anti-Qing movements from overseas, including the Tongmenghui. After the assassination of Song Jiaoren, widely attributed to Yuan, he led a failed Second Revolution and fled to Japan. He later took over junta leadership in [[Guangzhou]] and collaborated with the [[Soviet Union]] and the [[Chinese Communist Party]] to form the First United Front. His Three Principles of the People sought to modernize China through nationalism, democracy and the people's livelihood. The Republic of China calls him "Father of the Nation," and the People's Republic honors him as the "Forerunner of the Revolution."

Smallest bear species, found in the tropical forests of Southeast Asia. It is the only species in its genus, *Helarctos*, and stands nearly 70 cm at the shoulder, weighing 25–65 kg. Its name comes from the orange to cream-colored chest patch. The most arboreal of all bears, it sleeps in trees. It is an omnivore, eating [[Termite|termites]], ants, bees, honey and fruit, and does not hibernate. Heavy [[Deforestation|deforestation]] and poaching threaten it, and its global population is estimated to have declined by 35% since the 1990s. It is listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List.

Atmospheric optical phenomenon, also called a parhelion, in which bright spots appear on either side of the Sun. Sun dogs typically appear as a pair of patches about 22° to the left and right of the Sun. They are caused by refraction of sunlight by plate-shaped hexagonal ice crystals in high cirrus clouds, which act as prisms with a minimum deflection of 22°. They are red on the side nearest the Sun and are most conspicuous when the Sun is near the horizon. They are related to the [[Halo (optical phenomenon)|22° halo]], which forms a ring at roughly the same angular distance from the Sun.

Family of small, slender Old World passerine birds, which also includes the spiderhunters. The family Nectariniidae has 152 species in 16 genera, ranging through most of Africa, the Middle East, South Asia, Southeast Asia, southern China, [[Indonesia]], New Guinea and northern Australia. Most species feed largely on nectar, usually perching to feed, though some hover like a [[Hummingbird|hummingbird]], a resemblance produced by convergent evolution with the hummingbirds of the Americas and the [[Honeyeater|honeyeaters]] of Australia. Males of most species are brilliantly iridescent and have longer tails. Both sexes catch insects and spiders, especially when feeding young. Spiderhunters, restricted to Asia, have drab brown plumage in both sexes.

Austronesian language spoken mainly by the Sundanese people in western [[Java]], Indonesia. It has approximately 32 million native speakers, about 15% of Indonesia's population. Linguist Robert Blust considers it closely related to the Malayic languages. Until 1600 AD it was the state language of several kingdoms, including Sunda, Galuh and Pajajaran, and it was heavily influenced by [[Sanskrit]]. The earliest documents use the Old Sundanese script. Pegon script came with Islam, and the Latin script, introduced by Europeans, is used for most modern literature. The Priangan dialect, spoken around [[Bandung]], is the most widely spoken and is taught in schools in West Java and Banten. Speakers have settled beyond Java, including in Lampung, [[Taiwan]] and [[Japan]].

Mangrove forest in the [[Ganges|Ganges]] Delta, the world's largest mangrove forest, covering 10,277 sq km. It lies where the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers meet the [[Bay of Bengal]], extending from India's West Bengal to Bangladesh's Khulna Division. Four protected areas are UNESCO World Heritage Sites: three in [[Bangladesh]] and Sundarbans National Park in India. The forest supports 453 fauna species, including 290 bird, 120 fish, 42 mammal, 35 reptile and eight amphibian species. Cyclone Sidr in 2007 damaged around 40% of the forest, and Cyclone Aila in 2009 affected at least 100,000 people. Rising salinity from sea level rise threatens the forest, and a 2016 UNESCO report expected further damage from the coal-fired Rampal Power Station.

Day of the week between Saturday and Monday, a day of rest in most Western countries and part of the weekend. Its English name derives from Old English *sunnandæg*, a translation of the Latin *dies solis*, "day of the sun." For most Christians it is the Lord's Day, the day of Christ's resurrection, observed for worship and rest. It is the first day of the week in the [[United States]], [[Canada]], [[Japan]] and parts of South America, and in the Islamic, Hebrew and many traditional calendars, though ISO 8601 places it seventh. In some Arab countries it is a weekday.

Device that tells the time of day from the position of the Sun's shadow on a marked dial. In its narrowest sense it consists of a flat dial plate and a gnomon, whose shadow aligns with hour lines as the Sun moves across the sky. The style, the time-telling edge of the gnomon, must be parallel to Earth's axis for accuracy throughout the year, and its angle from horizontal equals the sundial's [[Latitude|latitude]]. Sundials show local solar time, so clock time requires corrections for the equation of time, which can be as great as 16 minutes, 33 seconds, and for the difference between the local [[Longitude|longitude]] and that of the official [[Time zone|time zone]]. Forms include horizontal, vertical, equatorial, polar and analemmatic dials. The earliest known examples date to ancient Egypt around 1500 BCE.

Portion of the electromagnetic radiation emitted by the Sun and received by Earth, including visible, [[Infrared|infrared]] and [[Ultraviolet|ultraviolet]] light. It takes about 8.3 minutes to reach Earth. Scattered and filtered by the atmosphere, it arrives as daylight, and as sunshine when not blocked by clouds. Sources estimate a global average of between 164 watts and 340 watts per square meter over a 24-hour day. Sunlight drives [[Photosynthesis|photosynthesis]] and enables vitamin D synthesis, but its ultraviolet radiation is also a mutagen and can cause sunburn.

Indian actor, filmmaker and former politician who works in [[Hindi]] films, known for his angry action-hero persona. He debuted in *Betaab* (1983) and won the Filmfare Award for Best Actor for *Ghayal* (1990). He had major hits with *Border* (1997) and *Gadar: Ek Prem Katha* (2001). After more than a decade of setbacks, his comeback *Gadar 2* (2023) became the highest-grossing film of his career. He represented Gurdaspur in the Lok Sabha as a member of the [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] from 2019 to 2024.

Canadian-American actress, model and media personality who works in [[Hindi]] films. Before entering mainstream film she worked in the North American adult film industry, and she was named Penthouse Pet of the Year in 2003. She appeared on the Indian reality show *Bigg Boss* in 2011 and made her Bollywood debut in the erotic thriller *Jism 2* (2012). Later films include *Jackpot* (2013) and *Ragini MMS 2* (2014). She has hosted *MTV Splitsvilla* and posed for a PETA campaign encouraging pet owners to spay and neuter their animals.

Daily disappearance of the Sun below the horizon as Earth rotates. It is defined as the moment the upper limb of the Sun disappears below the horizon, and atmospheric refraction means the solar disk is then about one diameter below it. Sunset occurs about once every 24 hours everywhere except near the poles, and the Sun sets due west at both [[Equinox|equinoxes]]. Civil [[Twilight|twilight]] lasts until the Sun is 6 degrees below the horizon, and night begins at 18 degrees. Beyond the Arctic and Antarctic Circles, the Sun may not set for 24 hours or more during polar day.

Annual championship game of the [[National Football League|NFL]], established by a 1966 merger agreement with the American Football League. The first game was played in 1967, and the name "Super Bowl" was adopted in 1969. The winning team receives the Vince Lombardi Trophy. The seven most-watched broadcasts in American television history are Super Bowls, and commercial airtime during the game is the most expensive of the year. The [[New England Patriots]] and [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] share the record for most wins, with six each.

Platform video game from 1985, developed and published by [[Nintendo]] for the [[Nintendo Entertainment System]]. Directed and produced by [[Shigeru Miyamoto]], it follows Mario as he crosses the Mushroom Kingdom to rescue Princess Toadstool from King Koopa, later named Bowser. Players move right through side-scrolling stages, collecting coins and power-ups such as the Super Mushroom and Fire Flower. Credited with helping revive the video game industry after the 1983 crash, it has sold more than 58 million copies worldwide. It began the *Super Mario* franchise, which includes an animated series and films.

Home video game console developed and marketed by [[Nintendo]], known as the Super Famicom in Japan. Released in Japan on November 21, 1990, and in North America on August 23, 1991, it was Nintendo's second programmable home console, after the [[Nintendo Entertainment System]]. Its 16-bit hardware included Mode 7 and eight-channel audio, and it competed mainly with the [[Sega Genesis]]. More than 1,700 games were released for it, and Nintendo sold 49.1 million units, the best-selling fourth-generation home console. Nintendo discontinued it in 1999, and it remains popular among collectors and retro gamers.
